bottom_line: Every future stops this line somewhere before 2031, and in every one the first part to fail is a site or supplier already on the risk list. Three actions pay off in every future: confirm the internal numbers the results rest on, test a 30-day manual fallback at both plants and both sole suppliers, and start qualifying a second maker of cold heads (the part that keeps a magnet cold) by the second quarter of 2027.
where_we_are_heading: On 11 Oct 2026 the indicators leaned toward trade costs rising without anything being cut off, and toward helium still limiting shipments. In the latest daily count, on 4 Oct 2026, four ships crossed the Gulf strait against a typical 85. Helium is bought on allocation letters, no export-control listing names wire or cold heads, and no 3 tesla sealed magnet has been cleared. Of the 12 indicators, 10 lean that way and two lean neither way. Neither question has been answered yet.
what_fails_first: In the future the indicators lean toward, the United States magnet plant runs out of helium on hand first, in the winter of 2028 to 2029. A grid curtailment or a flood cuts power to the liquefier and closes the trailer road while the next container is still in transit. Any hurricane season from 2027 could bring this forward. The China plant's helium queue fails second, in the first half of 2028. If an export-control listing comes first, the China plant stops in the second half of 2027 because its supply of logic parts is cut off. If helium stops limiting shipments, a single Japanese cold head stops both plants.
what_it_costs: In the future the indicators lean toward, the United States plant stops once for 30 to 45 days and a quarter of Western installs run more than 30 days late. Market share does not move, because every supplier is short of helium at the same time. The most expensive futures are the two where a part is cut off. In one, the China plant stops for the export license queue plus the time it takes to rehire, and Asian market share moves within one tender cycle. In the other, both plants stop for most of 18 months, installed magnets warm up, and Europe's replacement peak goes to competitors.
right_in_every_future: Confirm the Placeholder numbers now: days of helium on hand, backup power, the helium a sealed magnet draws in testing (in liters), the China plant's logic stock in weeks, where the cold-head maker is located, and its parent company's share of revenue from MR. Test a 30-day manual fallback with the wire mill and the cold-head maker taking part, because a 35-day systems outage pushes the line past the 30-day limit in all four futures, wherever each future's first failure already sits. Keep an offline, restore-tested copy of the design record. Start qualifying a second cold-head maker by the second quarter of 2027, once Sourcing names one with a letter of intent.
right_only_if_the_lean_holds: Keep more days of helium on hand at the United States plant than a container's hold time plus the 10-day grid rebuild, and put the liquefier on backup power, both before the winter of 2028. These pay off only in the futures where helium still limits shipments, which is where the indicators lean, and they only add carrying cost if sealed magnets take most new builds. Stock at the China plant is a bet on an export-control listing and must be bought before the truce notice, first read as 10 Nov 2026. A multi-year agreement with the cold-head maker's parent company is a bet on the parent leaving the business, and it does not help if an export license is refused.
one_action_waiting: Confirm the Placeholder numbers. The work costs only phone calls, named owners in Logistics, Site operations, Engineering and Sourcing hold it, and until it is done every other action on this page is sized to a synthetic number.
